newsitem.title: PERU: Peru says Brady deal to cut gov't debt to $21 bln.
newsitem.headline: Peru says Brady deal to cut gov't debt to $21 bln.

text.p: Peru's Prime Minister Alberto Pandolfi told Congress late Thursday the government's ongoing Brady bond negotiations with commercial creditors would likley reduce the government's medium- and long-term foreign debt to $21.258 billion, state news agency Andina reported.

"The Brady negotiation reduces the debt by $5.409 billion, so that the public foreign debt total would be $21.258 billion," Pandolfi said, adding that the latter figure included the new debt necessary to cover the initial cost of the start-up of the Brady plan.
The government has said the Brady deal's reduction is being negotiated on a total of $10.56 billion -- the bulk of the government's commercial debt.
However, market and independent sources put the commercial debt around $8.4 billion, and estimate a 40-50 percent reduction on this.
Economy and Finance Minister Jorge Camet has said the initial cost of the Brady Plan would be about $1.5 billion.
According to latest Central Reserve Bank figures, the country's overall foreign debt was $32.445 billion at the end of March.
This total debt figure includes both government and corporate short-, medium- and long-term debt.
The government is still negotiating with creditor banks to finalize bond selections under the Brady Plan.
Peru had announced a July 31 deadline for banks to choose their bond options and an August 9 date for the government to accept these formally.
However, the negotiations have dragged on in recent weeks without an official explanation for the delay.
Camet said last month the majority of the 400 creditor banks involved in the deal were tending towards the FLIRB bonds under the options offered in the Brady plan.
Peru reached a preliminary Brady agreement with its bank creditors last October.
